newsitem.title: USA: Omnicare sets Q3 charge for setlement.
newsitem.headline: Omnicare sets Q3 charge for setlement.

text.p: Omnicare Inc said Wednesday it will take a third quarter charge to establish a reserve of $6.3 million for the estimated costs and legal and other expenses associated with resolving the previously announced federal investigation of Home Pharmacy Services Inc, the company's institutional pharmacy subsidiary.

Omnicare said it has reached a tentative settlement, subject to final federal and State governmental approvals, with the U.S. Attorney's office in the Southern District of Illinois regarding the investigation of its Belleville, Ill., subsidiary.

Omnicare said the settlement, when completed, is not expected to result in any criminal charges against Home Pharmacy Services. Additionally, Home Pharmacy Services is expected to continue to participate in government reimbursement programs under the terms of the tentative settlement.
As previously announced, in May 1996 the company became aware of a government investigation of Home Pharmacy Services and certain individuals employed there at that time.
Omnicare said it has been informed that Home Pharmacy Services is the sole focus of the investigation and neither Omnicare nor any of its other operating units are targets of the inquiry.

Home Pharmacy Services was acquired by Omnicare in 1992. The pharmacy operation accounted for less than 3 percent of Omnicare's total sales and earnings in the second quarter of 1997 when it reported pretax income of $25.8 million and net income of $15.7 million before acquisition-related expenses on revenues of $203.1 million.
